name: Company Profile

inputs.name: Purpose: pitch, buyer profile, target profile or interview prep

steps.title: Scope the ask
steps.detail: A profile for a sell-side pitch, a buyer list and an interview answer emphasise different things. Fix the purpose first.

steps.title: Describe the business
steps.detail: What the company sells, to whom, how it makes money, segment split with revenue/EBITDA by segment.

steps.title: Build the financial snapshot
steps.detail: 3-year revenue, EBITDA, margins, leverage, FCF — with period labels and the source filing for each.

steps.title: Map ownership and management
steps.detail: Top shareholders, free float, CEO/CFO tenure, any activist or PE presence.

steps.title: Add market context
steps.detail: Trading multiples vs peers, 52-week range, recent news and broker sentiment where public.

steps.title: Pressure-test the page
steps.detail: Would an MD scan this in 60 seconds and find nothing to red-pen? Check formatting, footing and sources.

steps.title: Delegate 1
steps.detail: Gathering filings, investor decks and recent news into a source pack

steps.title: Delegate 2
steps.detail: Extracting segment splits and 3-year financials into a table

steps.title: Delegate 3
steps.detail: Drafting the business description from the 10-K

steps.title: Delegate 4
steps.detail: Compiling the management and shareholder lists

sections.name: Profile
sections.detail: Scale, per share, cash generation and balance sheet on one page — the tab you actually read

sections.name: Income Statement
sections.detail: Five years as filed, with growth and margin sub-rows computed as live formulas

sections.name: Balance Sheet
sections.detail: Five years as filed, with a conditional-red assets-less-liabilities-and-equity check

sections.name: Cash Flow
sections.detail: Five years as filed, with free cash flow computed in the workbook

sections.name: Filings
sections.detail: The 10-Ks and 10-Qs the numbers came out of

sections.name: Sources
sections.detail: Every figure resolved to tag, period, form, accession and an EDGAR link

outputs.sourcePolicy: SEC EDGAR XBRL company facts only. Original filings beat restated comparatives. A line the filer did not tag prints an em dash and is named in the gap list — blank never means zero.

verification.description: Financials tie to the filing (right period, right currency, right units)
Segment definitions match the company’s own reporting, not a generic split
Ownership data is current — stale shareholder lists are a classic error
News items are real and dated; no hallucinated events
Segment revenue sums to total revenue
The page reads top-down: most important facts first
No unexplained jargon a first-year wouldn’t know

humanCheckpoints: What the "so what" of this company is for your specific purpose
Which 3-4 facts lead the page and which go to footnotes
How to characterise the company’s competitive position honestly

display.jobToBeDone: Build a banker-grade one-pager on any company, fast.
